statement: For independent random variables, the relation 'X beats Y', meaning P(X > Y) > 1/2, is transitive.
definitions: X, Y, Z are mutually independent real-valued random variables; 'X beats Y' means P(X > Y) > 1/2; the claim is that X beats Y and Y beats Z together imply X beats Z.
ground_truth_witness: Roll three independent fair six-sided dice with faces A = (2,2,4,4,9,9), B = (1,1,6,6,8,8), C = (3,3,5,5,7,7). Exact enumeration of the 36 equally likely ordered face pairs in each comparison gives P(A > B) = 20/36 = 5/9, P(B > C) = 5/9, and P(C > A) = 5/9, each strictly greater than 1/2, so A beats B, B beats C, and C beats A: the beating relation cycles (Steinhaus-Trybula paradox, realized by nontransitive dice).
reference_authority: published counterexample (book-cited), verified per partB_feasibility records
book_citation: J. M. Stoyanov, Counterexamples in Probability, Wiley, 1987 (3rd ed., Dover, 2013); section on diverse properties of random variables (the Steinhaus-Trybula non-transitivity of the relation P(X > Y) > 1/2); example number not pinned from freely available sources.

skeptic.objection: False; witness verified by exact enumeration: P(A>B) = P(B>C) = P(C>A) = 20/36 = 5/9 with no ties. The statement should pin that the three variables are mutually independent and what transitivity means; with that pin it is unambiguous. Solver must exhibit explicit distributions and compute three probabilities (Efron/Steinhaus-Trybula style), a small but real construction. No roster/surplus overlap.
